question.text: Is vitamin D deficiency a feature of pediatric celiac disease?

medgemma_4b.clinical_reasoning: Vitamin D deficiency is a known complication of celiac disease in children. This is due to malabsorption of fat-soluble vitamins, including vitamin D, in the small intestine. While not all children with celiac disease will be vitamin D deficient, it is a common finding.
medgemma_4b.critical_evidence: Vitamin D deficiency is a known complication of celiac disease in children due to malabsorption.
medgemma_4b.differential_considered: Other causes of vitamin D deficiency (e.g., insufficient sun exposure, dietary insufficiency) were considered, but the presence of celiac disease makes vitamin D deficiency a more likely and relevant consideration in this context.

This malabsorption can lead to hypocalcemia, rickets, and other vitamin D-related complications, especially in children with untreated or poorly managed celiac disease.
